sources.journal: Journal of Plastic, Reconstructive & Aesthetic Surgery 96:123–128
sources.institution: Wenzhou Medical University and collaborating institutions

sources.limitations: PubMed direct open returned a browser challenge; primary indexed metadata inspected. Detailed anatomical figures/full methods were not available; this source cannot carry the authority decision.

sources.title: The dorsal flap of the first web
sources.journal: Journal of Hand Surgery (British and European Volume) 28(2):121–124
sources.relevant_anatomy: Dorsal first web; vascular communication involving index and thumb
sources.claim: A dorsal first-web flap can use regional vascular communication. Surgical flap survival establishes blood supply, not a native thumb-joint skin driver.
sources.limitations: Flap transposition changes attachments. Vascular continuity is direct evidence for perfusion only; no native skin trajectory or exact collar mapping.
sources.access: Primary publisher abstract and clinical introduction
sources.commercial_use_relevance: N/A — research citation only; no external figure or asset incorporated

sources.title: Regional first web flap used to cover the amputated stump of the thumb
sources.journal: Journal of Plastic Surgery and Hand Surgery 46(2):128–131
sources.relevant_anatomy: Radiodorsal index MCP surface toward dorsal first web
sources.claim: The reported flap donor extends from radiodorsal index MCP toward the dorsal first web. This establishes an adjacent surface corridor, not native CMC/MCP coupling at the model ring.
sources.limitations: Donor design is at index MCP, whereas the model ring projects well along the proximal phalanx. Mobilization after surgery does not measure intact regional skin displacement.
sources.commercial_use_relevance: N/A — research citation only; no external figure or asset incorporated

sources.title: The anatomy and function of Cleland’s ligaments
sources.institution: University Medical Center Groningen; University of Manchester
sources.evidence_type: Cadaver microdissection; 20 fresh-frozen digits and four Thiel-preserved fingers for dynamics
sources.relevant_anatomy: Lateral digital skin anchors; proximal phalanx/PIP relationship
sources.claim: Lateral cutaneous attachments anchor digital skin through flexion and extension. Origins include phalangeal, tendon-sheath and extensor-associated fascia; fibre orientation and tension change with finger motion.
sources.limitations: Fresh-frozen sample: six little, eight ring, six middle fingers; not an index/thumb sample. The mesh contains no dermis, fascia or ligament layers, so a surface vertex cannot be declared a specific ligament insertion.
sources.access: Primary full-text university PDF; methods, results and dynamics inspected
sources.commercial_use_relevance: N/A — research citation only; no external figure or asset incorporated

sources.title: Grayson Ligament: A Revised Description of its Anatomy and Function
sources.institution: University Medical Center Groningen; University of Manchester
sources.evidence_type: 20-digit cadaver microdissection plus Thiel-preserved hand dynamics
sources.relevant_anatomy: Volar digital skin/fat and flexor-sheath trabecular network
sources.claim: A volar fascial network links tendon-sheath adventitia to skin and fat. Its orientation changes during finger flexion, permitting local fat-pad adaptation.
sources.limitations: Long-finger analogy, not direct index/first-web thumb motion measurement. Does not identify an individual model skin vertex as Grayson tissue or distinguish CMC from MCP effects.
sources.access: Primary indexed abstract and university full text
sources.commercial_use_relevance: N/A — research citation only; no external figure or asset incorporated

sources.title: The dorsal wrinkle ligaments of the proximal interphalangeal joint
sources.evidence_type: Cadaver dorsal digital skin attachment study
sources.claim: Dorsal skin at the PIP has structured wrinkle attachments. This supports a local digital skin role as a candidate for nearby dorsal proximal-phalanx surface.
sources.limitations: The model ring is proximal to PIP, not proven to coincide with a crease; sample does not register this specific index ring. No thumb opposition coupling measurement.
sources.access: Primary indexed abstract; author manuscript metadata cross-check
sources.commercial_use_relevance: N/A — research citation only; no external figure or asset incorporated

sources.title: Predictors of successful outcomes in first web space contracture release
sources.evidence_type: Clinical functional outcomes after first-web contracture release
sources.claim: After first-web contracture release, restored abduction and persistent opposition deficits differ. Real first-web tissue matters functionally for opposition, but the study does not isolate native skin drivers.
sources.limitations: Pathological/reconstructed webs, small follow-up sample; not normal skin tracking. No index-ring registration and no separation of CMC versus MCP contribution.
sources.commercial_use_relevance: N/A — research citation only; no external figure or asset incorporated

sources.title: Robust Identification of Three-Dimensional Thumb and Index Finger Kinematics With a Minimal Set of Markers
sources.relevant_anatomy: Skin-marker passive motion relative to skeletal kinematics
sources.claim: Skin-marker passive motion complicates skeletal kinematics. Fewer markers and nail clusters reduce artifacts; joint kinematics alone do not establish a local skin deformation field.
sources.limitations: No absolute gold standard and no spatially resolved commissure/thenar skin-displacement map. It cannot authorize either thumb group at the collar.
sources.access: Primary indexed abstract and PMC full text
sources.commercial_use_relevance: N/A — research citation only; no external figure or asset incorporated

level_scope: Levels apply to the narrow anatomical claim described, not to an exact model mapping. LEVEL_A source count is not a count of authorized vertices.
research_method: Focused primary literature searches: first-web morphology/flaps/contracture function; lateral and volar digital attachments; dorsal PIP skin; skin-marker artifact. No ordinary 3D model, AI image, blog, forum or commercial illustration supplies anatomical authority.
access_limitations: S1 cannot supply an inspected detailed boundary; explicitly downgraded to LEVEL_C.
No reviewed source maps normal skin displacement at these exact model points separately to CMC opposition and thumb MCP flexion.
excluded_scope_examples: Tonkin 2015 web measurements concern second/third/fourth webs and are not first-web authority.
Secondary surgical reviews and commercial atlas pages were search leads only.
